Commercial Cleaning Sydney

Commercial spaces need a cleaning plan that fits how the site operates.

Visit main website ↗

Start with the site, not a standard package

A small office, customer-facing store and busy warehouse all have different requirements. Effective cleaning begins with understanding the space, foot traffic, surfaces and business activity.

  • Entrance and reception
  • Shared facilities
  • Floors and surfaces
  • Site-specific requirements

Three building blocks of a cleaning plan

Use a straightforward process to establish priorities and service expectations.

Identify regular tasks

Note surfaces, amenities, shared kitchens, floors and high-touch points that need frequent attention.

Set the right frequency

Decide which tasks are daily, weekly or periodic based on how the space is used.

Confirm the scope

Request clear inclusions, exclusions, supplies, access arrangements and reporting expectations.

Westlink Commercial Cleaning • Sydney

Office Cleaning Sydney

A clear approach to clean desks, meeting rooms, reception areas and shared spaces.

Visit main website ↗

Build a plan around how your office is used

Divide your workplace into zones such as workstations, meeting rooms, kitchens, washrooms, reception and shared spaces.

  • Workstations
  • Meeting rooms
  • Kitchens and amenities
  • Reception areas

Focus on the places people notice

A good plan addresses busy shared spaces without disrupting the workday.

Shared touchpoints

Pay attention to shared desks, door handles, kitchens and areas with high daily use.

Floors and presentation

Maintain entrances, reception and meeting spaces appropriate to the premises.

Access and timing

Document suitable cleaning windows, key access and on-site contact arrangements.

Review outcomes regularly

Use a simple cleaning checklist and a clear feedback process to identify recurring concerns. Adjust the scope if work patterns, occupancy or building requirements change.

Westlink Commercial Cleaning • Sydney

Cleaning Quality Guide

Practical ways to define and review cleaning standards.

Visit main website ↗

Define expectations before judging results

A cleaning service can only be assessed consistently when the scope is clear. List each room, task, frequency and any exclusions.

  • Room-by-room scope
  • Clear cleaning frequency
  • Documented exclusions
  • Point of contact

Four things you can observe

Use these checks to structure feedback rather than relying only on a general impression.

Entry and reception

Are customer-facing areas tidy and presentable?

Kitchen and washrooms

Are agreed amenities tasks being completed?

Floors and surfaces

Are bins, floors and frequently touched areas attended to?

Turn observations into action

Record findings, agree on follow-up actions and revisit the checklist when your building use or occupancy changes. A designated contact makes communication simpler.
